26468e87-ca03-4c49-a588-042ff7a7ee45.name: Dawson Shamblin
26468e87-ca03-4c49-a588-042ff7a7ee45.occasionNotes:
Phone call with Dawson Shamblin - Linkedin - SVP at Kanbrick (Was on founding team) - Kanbrick is a direct descendent of Berkshire Hathaway, with a long-term hold investment model in lower-mid market space
Main Points (More from our Claude transcribed conversation summary below)
He sits on IC, mainly works in post-acq environment. Very friendly. Very fired up by what we're doing.
Lot to work with here - but ultimately, while we are fully aligned with their vision / strategy, Kanbrick plays at a very different threshold $10M-50M EBITDA range. They also leverage the "Kanbrick community" (YPO-esque forum for CEOs, 4000 members nationwide) as sourcing element for their fund. See 250-300 deals / year from this pipeline, invest in 1-2 annually.
He's very bullish on the idea of finding a truly great business with a "builder CEO" that is looking for true partners in the trenches - partners that can provide a little capital, but mainly horsepower. Might be a 60 something that doesn't have chops in tech, but wants to continue pushing the business forward.
Interesting Idea - Don't be unoriginal in this space. Given true long-term vision, there's a lot of opportunity to truly partner with a "builder CEO" who needs operational capacity partnership and isn't adept at growing nascent challenges (e.g., AI). Could do a 60 us / 40 them structure where we provide eventual succession and near-term operational capacity in whatever they face that they view as existentially concerning. Interesting, but not sure we want to be that novel.
Our stewardship pitch will only go so far. With a real business / sharp seller, we will need to play on the trust element mixed with grit. Any "builder CEO" of a truly good business won't be seeking to toss the "hot potato" because he doesn't like his son in law. We'll need to establish trust alongside horsepower. He mentioned that it's "very valuable to meet them with empathy - leaning on mutual leadership-oriented scars." This can be from our time at A&M / Bain, or more likely from RCA / Revelyst.
"Growth heals all" - for a truly good business with a defensible moat that is ripe for conquest, then we won't have to worry about whether AI will steal "Pam in Accounting's job." Firing at any family based entity is a poison pill.
